findings.headline: Keep format as createSignal's value instead of a derived computation.
findings.why: Solid 1.x stored a function passed to createSignal as the initial value. Solid 2.0.3 treats createSignal(fn) as a derived signal and calls fn, so the value becomes whatever fn returns.
findings.guidance: If the signal holds a function (a handler, a component, a formatter), wrap it: createSignal(() => format). Setter calls that already pass () => nextFn keep working. If the intent was a value computed from other signals, this is the new derived form and nothing changes.

findings.headline: Check this createStore(fn) call, which Solid 2 runs as a derived store.
findings.why: Solid 1.x stored a function passed to createStore as the initial value. Solid 2.0.3 treats createStore(fn) as a derived store and calls fn, so the value becomes whatever fn returns.
findings.guidance: A store's initial value must be an object or array. If this function computes the state from other signals, this is the new derived store form and takes a seed as the second argument; otherwise pass the object itself.
